full_judgment:
Obaidul Hassan J. This criminal appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 14.07.2014 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Death Reference No.33 of 2009 with Criminal Appeal No.4171 of 2010 with Jail Appeal No.47 of 2010 accepting the death reference of the condemned appellant Mohammad Jabed Jahangir (hereinafter referred to as Jabed/ appellant/ accused appellant) and thereby affirming the judgment and order dated 03.05.2009 passed by the learned Judge of the Divisional Druta Bichar Tribunal, Chittagong (hereinafter re erred to as the trial Court) in Druta Bichar Case No.51 of 2008 convicting the appellant under section 302 of the Penal Code, 1860 and sentencing him to death. 

 2. The prosecution case, in short, is that one Hazi Md. Shahidur Rahman lodged First Information Report (shortly, FIR) with Bakalia Police Station on 02.04.2007 against accused appellant under section 302/201 of the Penal Code, 1860 alleging, inter alia, that on 22.02.2007 the appellant made an agreement on a 150 Taka Stamp paper with the informant Hazi Md. Shahidur Rahrrian to live in his 4 storied building (Mim House, Chittagong), South unit at a monthly rental of Tk.2500.00 from 01.03.2007 with his family. As the said house was vacant, Md. Jabed Jahangir took possession of the same with his family and other belongings on 25.02.2007 and began to reside as husband and wife. Jabed Jahangir said to the informant and his gate keeper that he used to serve in Shahin brothers at Asadgonj. On 02.04.2007 bad smell was spreading from the building of the informant who directed his gate keeper to look into the matter. Gate keeper Mohammad Ali searched everywhere in the building and guessed that the bad smell was coming out from the South unit of 3rd Floor but the room was locked. Maid servant Hasina says that perhaps Jabed Jahangir and his wife went to Dhaka. Gate Keeper Mohammad Ali disclosed that on 31.03.2007 Saturday at noon, Jabed Jahangir alone went out leaving his wife and thereafter, he did not come back. After Magrib prayer the informant along with his ten-ant Abbas and neighbour Md. Eakub, Md. Shafiq broke the lock of the room and entered therein and found the dead body of the wife of Jabed Jahangir lying on the bed pressed by the mattress. The informant instantly informed the matter to the local police station. He came to know from maid servant Hasina that Jabed Jahangir used to call his wife as Ria. Police came from Thana, prepared the inquest report of the dead body and sent the dead body to Chitttagong Medical College Hospital Morgue for Postmortem examination. After query, the informant came to know that Jabed Jahangir did not mention his father's name and address correctly in the agreement and his father's correct name is Harun-or-Rashid, who lives at Chandgaon residential area with family. Accused Jabed Jahangir killed his wife Ria, kept the dead body under the mattress in the room and left the house on 31.03.2007 at noon keeping the room under lock and key and accordingly, the informant lodged the F.I.R. with Bakalia Thana, C.M.P. Chittagong, on 02.04.2007 on the basis of which police started investigation. 

 3. After investigation, police submitted charge sheet against the accused appellant Md. Jabed Jahangir under sections 302/ 201 of the Penal Code, 1860. 

 6. On the closure of the evidence of the prosecution witnesses and conclusion of trial, the Tribunal found Md. Jabed Jahangir guilty under section 302 of the Penal Code, 1860 and thereby, sentenced him to death by judgment dated 03.05.2009. 

 35. P. W.18, Md. Kaikislu, stated that on 03.05.2007 he was posted as S.I. at Bakalia Thana. On 02.04.2007, he took the charge of investigation of this case. During investigation he visited the place of occurrence and examined the docket. He examined the maid servant of Jabed Jahangir under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898. After investigation he submitted charge sheet being No. 104 dated 04.08.2007 under sections 302/201 of the Penal Code, 1860. 

 39. It is a settled principle of criminal case that the prosecution has to prove charge against the accused beyond reasonable doubt, but this principle is to some extent otherwise when the case is a wife killing case. In a wife killing case, when the wife was in custody of the accused, the accused has to explain how his wife met death and in absence of any such sufficient explanation from husband's side, it is presumed that the husband was responsible for his wife's death. It was held in Ilias Hussain (Md) vs. State [54 DLR (AD) 78] that, "It is well settled that when a wife met with an unnatural death while in custody of the husband and also while in his house the husband is to explain under what circumstance the wife met with her death." In the instant case, the appellant was absconding. The trial of the case was held in absentia. 

 42. From the materials on record, it appears that the appellant mohammad Jabed Jahangir is in the condemned cell for more that 14 (fourteen) years suffering the pangs of death. It was held in the case of Nazrul Islam (Md) vs. State reported in [66 DLR (AD) 199] that, "Lastly with regard to the period of time spent by the accused in the condemned cell, there are numerous decisions of this Division which shed light on this aspect. In general terms, it may be stated that the length of period spent by a convict in the condemned cell is not necessarily a ground for commutation of the sentence of death. However, where the period spent in the condemned cell is not due to any fault of the convict and where the period spent there is inordinately long, it may be considered as an extenuating ground sufficient for commutation of sentence of death." In view of the decision cited above as well as the circumstances of this case, we are of the view that justice would be sufficiently met if the sentence of death of the appellant Mohammad Jabed Jahangir be commuted to one of imprisonment for life.
